verifications.claim: Artemis program missions launch from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Artemis II mission is launching from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the historic Launch Complex 39B.'; R2: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida'; R8: 'using Launch Complex 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Artemis II (part of Artemis program) launches from LC-39B at KSC, Florida, implying program use.

verifications.claim: Launch Complex 39B (LC-39B) is located at Kennedy Space Center, Merritt Island, Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R7: 'Space Center on Merritt Island, Cape Canaveral'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm LC-39B at Kennedy Space Center, Florida; R7 specifies Merritt Island location of KSC.

verifications.claim: The rocket for Artemis program missions is Space Launch System (SLS).

verifications.evidence: R1/R2/R3/R5/R8: 'NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; R6: 'SLS rocket'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly identify SLS as the rocket for Artemis missions.

verifications.claim: The spacecraft for Artemis program missions is Orion Spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: Artemis II launched from Launch Complex 39B on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT' on 'April 1, 2026' from 'Launch Complex 39B'; R2: 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. EDT' from 'Launch Complex 39B'; R8: 'took off ... on April 1 ... from Launch Complex 39B'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm exact launch date, time, and site for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R3: 'first time since 1972'; R8: 'first humans back to the Moon in over 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe Artemis II as first crewed lunar mission since Apollo (1972), over 50 years prior to 2026.

verifications.claim: Launch Complex 39B is part of the launch site historically used for the Apollo and Space Shuttle programs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pad 39B ... starting with Apollo 10 ... 53 Space Shuttle launches'; R2: 'supported America’s major space programs ... Pad B saw the launch of NASA’s Artemis I ... primary launch pad'; R8: 'the same historic pad used for Apollo and Space Shuttle missions'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state LC-39B's history with Apollo and Shuttle programs.
